deep.reconstruction:
This page continues a set of lecture-style notes on classical entire-function theory (order, genus, Hadamard–Borel factorization). It is background for the functional-analysis material in this folder. Order is ω(f) = limsup log log M(r) / log r; genus is the smallest integer p such that f = e^{g} z^k ∏ E_p(z/a_n), with deg g ≤ p and Σ|a_n|^{-p-1} < ∞. The previous page proved genus ≤ order ≤ genus + 1.

(1) Examples illustrating that remark. For integer ω, e^{z^ω} has order ω and genus ω, so it attains the bound g = ω. For α > 1, ∏_n (1 − z/n^α) has zeros n^α with convergence exponent 1/α. Its order is therefore 1/α (Grothendieck writes 'à vérifier'). Its genus is 0, since Σ n^{-α} < ∞.

(2) Algebraic remark. The order satisfies ω(fg) ≤ max(ω(f), ω(g)). The same holds for sums and scalar multiples (the 'λ, sommes'). Hence, for fixed ρ, the entire functions of order < ρ form an algebra, and so do those of order ≤ ρ. A crossed-out start ('Donc, si f(z) = e^{P(z)} f_1') shows he was about to use this to absorb exponential factors.

(3) A coefficient criterion attributed to Hadamard. Let f(z) = Σ c_n z^n. If n^α |c_n|^{1/n} → 0, then |c_n| ≤ n^{-αn} eventually. By the coefficient formula for the order, ω = limsup n log n / log(1/|c_n|) ≤ 1/α. So f has order ≤ 1/α, and hence genus 0 when α > 1.

The next page uses this to prove a proposition: if the coefficients of f are dominated by those of a genus-0 function h, and Σ 1/|z_i| < ∞ over the zeros of f, then f has genus 0.
errors: The conclusion 'f est au plus de genre 1/2' cannot be literally right: the genus is an integer. The correct statement is 'order ≤ 1/α', which gives genus 0 when α > 1. Either the handwriting reads 1/α (the α resembling a 2), or this is a slip.
e^{z^ω} is an entire function only for integer ω. That is implicit here but not stated.
The order of the product (1/α) is left 'à vérifier'. It is correct: the order of a canonical product equals the convergence exponent of its zeros.

ideas.what: Examples showing genus = order and genus = 0 with non-integer order
ideas.modern_name: Order vs genus of entire functions; canonical products

deep.surprise_reason: These are standard textbook facts about the order and genus of entire functions, written up as course or study notes. There is nothing new and nothing left unfinished beyond a self-check ('à vérifier').
transcription_corrections: 'au plus de genre 1/2' should most likely read 'au plus d'ordre 1/α' (or 'de genre 0'). Mathematically the bound must be order ≤ 1/α.
'ainsi donc que les λ, sommes' is probably 'ainsi donc que [des] λ-[multiples et des] sommes', i.e. the closure of the class under linear combinations.
'dont l'ordre est < ρ donne (ou est ≤ ρ)' should read 'dont l'ordre est < ρ donné (ou est ≤ ρ)'.
